answer.rationale: The 18% cost-cut mandate and the incumbent's refusal to renegotiate this cycle make a status-quo renewal inconsistent with the primary objective. The low-cost vendor's quote reportedly meets the mandate on its own (c2), and c4 confirms a prior low-cost onboarding was quick with accurate invoicing — though c4 was framed as 'renegotiating with the incumbent,' so its transfer to a vendor switch should be weighted lightly. With the contract expiring in 14 days and no auto-renew, deferral (c5) is not viable here. I cannot afford a pure dual-sourcing ramp (c3) under a single-decision constraint. So I would switch primary to the low-cost vendor this cycle — but with a short structured guard: capped initial volume share on the new vendor, retained fallback with the incumbent on rolling terms, and an explicit review trigger tied to delivery KPIs. This minimizes TCO via the headline price reduction while containing delivery risk on a line already running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer.
